summary: Every course must be letter graded unless your advisor approves otherwise. You take the four core energy courses, the three foundational courses, 18 units of graduate ENERGY technical electives (courses from other departments are moved in with advisor approval), ENERGY 358 for teaching, 3 units of ENERGY 352, and either 6 units of ENERGY 361 research with an MS thesis or 6 more technical elective units. Research, teaching and seminar units are not technical electives. You need 45 units besides ENERGY 352, at most 6 of them research, and 49 units in all. Your advisor checks the 3.0 GPA and approves your program of study, which must span at least two disciplines.

program.why: Grading: "All required courses must be taken for a letter grade." "Complete all courses for a letter grade, unless otherwise approved." An approved exception is moved in by hand.

totals.label: 45 units besides ENERGY 352
totals.why: "Complete a 45-unit program of study" "Complete 3 units of ENERGY 352 (ESE Graduate Seminar). These units are required but do not count toward the 45-unit total." The 352 units still count toward the 49 in "Minimum Units in the Program: 49", so they are left out of the 45 only.

totals.label: At most 6 units of research
totals.why: "Research option: at least 39 units of coursework, with up to 6 units of research" ENERGY 361 is the MS research course; the other ENERGY research courses are research too.

Rn1JRlbu.why: "The MS program requires completion of seven mandatory courses, consisting of four core energy courses and three foundational courses." An introduction to the two rules that list those courses.

j30F1N0B.why: "Students complete technical courses totaling 18 elective units, which may include graduate-level courses in Energy Science and Engineering and related disciplines." "Course selections ... may include other relevant offerings across departments, subject to advisor approval." Graduate ENERGY courses count; others are moved in by hand. Research, teaching, seminars, industry-training reports and TGR are not technical courses: "Research option: at least 39 units of coursework, with up to 6 units of research"; ENERGY 352 units "do not count toward the 45-unit total".
